Three foll=w up thoughts: 
1) In cases where we can't tell complete stories, like your=sorting algorithm, we can presumably tell stories about 
certain features. A=d I guess this is what I was trying to claim about evolutionary theory; we c=n't hope to predict a 
priori which features will show up in which taxa or w=y humans evolved, but we can explain why sex ratios are about 
50:50. And in=such cases we can still distinguish between good and bad stories (the god e=planation or a group selection 
explanation vs fisher). 
But I guess th=s raises two questions: 
2) In such domains, which kinds of stories w=ll we be able to tell and which kinds won't we? Should we be striving for 
a=Darwin-like story of human culture? For a high level pseudocode-like story f=r how the mind works? Or are there 
other questions we should be asking? Wha= is the level of analysis we should be doing in these domains of 
research?&=bsp; 
3) And in such domains, how can we distinguish good from bad stories?=This seems like a particular problem in domains, 
like the social and biolog=cal science, where even the good stories are incomplete and never 100% accu=ate. But there 
are still better and worse stories. Currently, as you pointe= out, these fields seem rife with bad stories. How could we 
more systematic=lly distinguish the good from the bad, in such domains? Is there a conceptu=l tool or a litmus test they 
might be able to apply?

I didn't get to hear what your daughter does, but it sound=d like she has an interest in psychology. And in evolution. I

Financials: buy XLF call spreads 
Underweight positioning, buybacks resuming, positive momentum and strong fundamentals all indicate that there is still 
further upside potential in financials (more details below). Our financials sector specialist thinks XLF could have another 
20-25% upside given the many levers to the Trump Trade: less regulation, higher interest rates, higher vol, economic 
growth, loan growth, etc. The asset sensitive regional banks are more of a pure play on a rates move but we view the 
larger cap banks as having multi-pronged upside given the aforementioned points. 
That said, given the velocity and magnitude of the recent move and uncertainty around the impact and timing of 
Trump's policies, we believe options offer better risk-reward than being outright long financials stocks here. With flat 
call skew, "appearing" call spreads with upside knock-ins price well. 
Buy a 1 year XLF call spread for 2.6% premium 
Buy a 110% call 
Sell a 117.5% call with an at-expiry knock-in at 125% (call is not active unless XLF is 125% or higher at expiry) 
o Total premium is 2.6% 
o Gross max payoff if knock-in is triggered: 2.9x (7.5%/2.6%) 
o Gross max payoff if knock-in is not triggered: 5.7x (14.9%/2.6%) — you have upside up to 124.9% 
Post Election Flow Skews - Buyers of Health Care (via ETFs) and Financials (mainly ETFs) 
US Buyback Flows 
• 
Cons Disc, Technology and Financials are the largest 3 sectors for US buybacks (over 70% of execution). We are 
seeing a seasonal increase in buybacks as we come out of the low seasonal month of the year (October) and should see 
increased buyback executions until year-end, another source of upside for the Cons Disc, Technology and Financials 
sectors.
